vocabulary.definition: a higher-dimensional analogue of a sphere
vocabulary.example: Scientists theorize that the universe could be shaped like a hypersphere, curving back on itself in higher dimensions.

vocabulary.definition: relating to the universe or cosmos, especially as distinct from the earth
vocabulary.example: The cosmic microwave background radiation provides evidence for the Big Bang theory.

vocabulary.definition: a seemingly absurd or self-contradictory statement or proposition that when investigated may prove to be well founded or true
vocabulary.example: The concept of infinity in the universe presents various paradoxes that challenge our understanding of reality.

vocabulary.definition: the action of copying or reproducing something
vocabulary.example: In an infinite universe, the theory of replication suggests that there could be exact copies of individuals scattered across space.

vocabulary.definition: able to be tested or tried
vocabulary.example: The hypothesis about the shape of the universe being a hypersphere is currently not testable with our existing technology.

vocabulary.definition: the study of the fundamental nature of knowledge, reality, and existence
vocabulary.example: Contemplating the infinite nature of the universe leads us into the realm of science philosophy.
